content.p: Subdivision B—Applications for, and payment of, indemnity scheme payments

section.heading: Application for IBNR indemnity, high cost claim indemnity, run-off cover indemnity or allied health high cost claim indemnity

content.p: An application by an MDO or insurer for an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity must:
be made in writing using a form approved by the Chief Executive Medicare; and
be accompanied by the documents and other information required by the form approved by the Chief Executive Medicare.

section.heading: Payment date for IBNR indemnity, high cost claim indemnity, run-off cover indemnity or allied health high cost claim indemnity

content.p: Subject to subsections (2) and (2A), the Chief Executive Medicare must pay an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity that is payable to an MDO or insurer before the end of the month that immediately follows the month in which the MDO or insurer applies for the indemnity.
Payment will not be made until requested information is given
Subject to subsection (2A), if:
an MDO or insurer applies for an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity; and
the Chief Executive Medicare requests a person to give information under section 38 in relation to the application; and

the person does not give the Chief Executive Medicare the information requested before the end of the month that immediately follows the month in which the MDO or insurer applies for the indemnity; and
an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity is payable to the MDO or insurer;

the Chief Executive Medicare must pay the IBNR indemnity, the high cost claim indemnity, the run-off cover indemnity or the allied health high cost claim indemnity to the MDO or insurer before the end of the month that immediately follows the month in which the person gives the Chief Executive Medicare the requested information.
Application may be treated as withdrawn if requested information is not given
The Chief Executive Medicare may treat an application as having been withdrawn if:
the Chief Executive Medicare requests the MDO or insurer who made the application to give information under section 38 in relation to the application; and
the MDO or insurer does not give the information to the Chief Executive Medicare by the end of the day specified in the request.
The Chief Executive Medicare must notify the MDO or insurer if the Chief Executive Medicare treats the application as having been withdrawn.
Definitions
In this section:
month means one of the 12 months of the year.

section.heading: Application for exceptional claims indemnity or allied health exceptional claims indemnity

content.p: An application for an exceptional claims indemnity in relation to a qualifying liability that relates to a claim may be made by the person against whom the claim is or was made, or by a person acting on that person’s behalf.

An application for an allied health exceptional claims indemnity in relation to a qualifying allied health liability that relates to a claim may be made by the person against whom the claim is or was made, or by a person acting on that person’s behalf.
An application under subsection (1) or (1A) must:
be made in writing using a form approved by the Chief Executive Medicare; and
be accompanied by the documents and other information required by the form approved by the Chief Executive Medicare.
Subject to subsection (5), the application cannot be made more than 28 days after:
if the liability is under a judgment or order of a court—the date on which the judgment or order became or becomes a judgment or order that is not stayed and is not subject to appeal; or
if the liability is under a settlement of the claim—the date on which the settlement agreement was entered into; or
if the liability is some other kind of liability—the date on which the liability was incurred.
The Chief Executive Medicare may accept a late application if the Chief Executive Medicare considers that there are good reasons for doing so.
An application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of a decision of the Chief Executive Medicare not to accept a late application.
Note: Section 266 of the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 requires notification of a decision that is reviewable.

section.heading: Payment date for exceptional claims indemnity or allied health exceptional claims indemnity

content.p: Time by which application must be decided

Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the Chief Executive Medicare is to decide an application for an exceptional claims indemnity or an allied health exceptional claims indemnity on or before the end of the 21st day after the day on which the application is received by the Chief Executive Medicare.

If the Chief Executive Medicare requests a person to give information under section 38 in relation to an application for an exceptional claims indemnity or an allied health exceptional claims indemnity, the Chief Executive Medicare does not have to decide the application until the 21st day after the day on which the person gives the information to the Chief Executive Medicare.
If the Chief Executive Medicare has received, but not yet decided:
(a) an application (the certificate application) for the issue of a qualifying claim certificate or a qualifying allied health claim certificate in relation to a claim; and
(b) an application (the indemnity application) for an exceptional claims indemnity or allied health exceptional claims indemnity in relation to the same claim;
the Chief Executive Medicare does not have to decide the indemnity application until the Chief Executive Medicare has decided the certificate application.
Time by which payment must be made

If the Chief Executive Medicare decides to grant an application for an exceptional claims indemnity or an allied health exceptional claims indemnity, the Chief Executive Medicare must pay the indemnity to the applicant as soon as practicable after making that decision.
Subdivision C—Information gathering and record keeping

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may request information

content.p: If the Chief Executive Medicare believes on reasonable grounds that a person is capable of giving information that is relevant to determining:
whether an indemnity scheme payment is payable; or
the amount of the indemnity scheme payment that is payable; or
whether a qualifying claim certificate or qualifying allied health claim certificate should be issued, varied or revoked; or
the Commonwealth’s possible future liability to make indemnity scheme payments, or a particular kind of indemnity scheme payment;
the Chief Executive Medicare may request the person to give the Chief Executive Medicare the information.
Note 1: Failure to comply with the request is an offence (see section 45).
Note 2: Failure to comply may affect certain indemnity scheme payments: see sections 34I, 34ZZO and 37.
Without limiting subsection (1), any of the following persons may be requested to give information under that subsection:
an MDO;
an insurer;
a member, or former member, of an MDO;
a person who practises, or used to practise, a medical profession;
a person who is acting, or has acted, on behalf of a person covered by paragraph (ca);
the legal personal representative of a person covered by paragraph (c), (ca) or (cb).

Without limiting subsection (1), if the information sought by the Chief Executive Medicare is information relating to a matter in relation to which a person is required by section 39 or 40 to keep a record, the Chief Executive Medicare may request the person to give the information by giving the Chief Executive Medicare the record, or a copy of the record.
Without limiting paragraph (1)(d), the Chief Executive Medicare may request an MDO or insurer to give information under that paragraph on a periodic basis.
The request:
must be made in writing; and
must state what information must be given to the Chief Executive Medicare; and
may require the information to be verified by statutory declaration; and
must specify the day on or before which the information must be given; and
must contain a statement to the effect that a failure to comply with the request is an offence.
The day specified under paragraph (d) must be at least 28 days after the day on which the request is made.

section.heading: Main record keeping obligations

content.p: Records to be kept by person who applies for payment

A person who applies for an indemnity scheme payment, or a payment under regulations made for the purposes of section 27A (IBNR claims payments), 34AA (high cost claims payments), 34X (exceptional claims payments), 34ZN (run-off claims payments), 34ZZG (allied health high cost claims payments) or 34ZZZD (allied health exceptional claims payments), must keep records relevant to the following matters:
the payability of the payment;
the amount of the payment payable;
any amount paid to the person that results in a person being liable to pay an amount under section 24, 34T, 34ZJ or 34ZZZ;
any other matter specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to keep the records is an offence (see section 47).
Records to be kept by person who applies for a qualifying claim certificate or qualifying allied health claim certificate
A person who applies for the issue of a qualifying claim certificate or a qualifying allied health claim certificate in relation to a claim must keep records that are relevant to the following:
matters related to whether the criteria specified in subsection 34E(1) or 34ZZK(1) are satisfied in relation to the claim;
any other matter specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to keep the records is an offence (see section 47).
Records to be retained for certain period
The records must be retained for a period of 5 years (or any other period specified in the rules) starting on the day on which the records were created.
Note: Failure to retain the records is an offence (see section 47).
Rules regarding additional matters
Rules made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(d) or (1A)(b) must not commence earlier than 14 days after the day on which the rules are registered on the Federal Register of Legislation.

section.heading: Certain insurers and MDOs to keep additional records

content.p: Records to be kept
An insurer or MDO that applies for an IBNR indemnity must keep records that are relevant to the following matters:
determining its IBNR exposure as at the end of a financial year;
any other matter specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to keep the records is an offence (see section 47).
Records to be retained for certain period
The records must be retained for a period of 5 years (or any other period specified in the rules) starting on the day on which the records were created.
Note: Failure to retain the records is an offence (see section 47).
Rules regarding additional matters
Rules made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(e) must not commence earlier than 14 days after the day on which the rules are registered on the Federal Register of Legislation.
Subdivision D—Overpayments of the indemnities

section.heading: Recovery of overpayments

content.p: This section applies if an amount is paid by way of an indemnity scheme payment and:
the amount of indemnity scheme payment is not payable; or
the amount paid is greater than the amount of the indemnity scheme payment that was payable.
(2) The amount overpaid is:
the whole of the amount paid if paragraph (1)(a) applies; or
the difference between the amount that was paid and the amount that was payable if paragraph (1)(b) applies.
(3) The amount overpaid is a debt due to the Commonwealth by the liable person. For this purpose the liable person is:

if the indemnity scheme payment was an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity—the MDO or insurer to which the payment was made; or
if the indemnity scheme payment was an exceptional claims indemnity—the person who is the liable person under subsection 34R(2); or
if the indemnity scheme payment was an allied health exceptional claims indemnity—the person who is the liable person under subsection 34ZZX(2).

Note 1: For paragraphs (b) and (c), if the exceptional claims indemnity or allied health exceptional claims indemnity is not dealt with as required by section 34Q or 34ZZW, the whole amount of the indemnity is a debt owed by the recipient, and no amount is recoverable under this section (see subsections 34Q(6) to (8) and 34ZZW(6) to (8)).
Note 2: For paragraphs (b) and (c), if:
the recipient and the practitioner are not the same person; and
the practitioner becomes the liable person;
then (subject to subsections 34R(3) and 34ZZX(3)), the recipient ceases to be the liable person, and the amount overpaid must instead be recovered from the practitioner.
The amount overpaid may be recovered:
by action by the Chief Executive Medicare against the liable person in a court of competent jurisdiction; or
by deduction from the amount of an IBNR indemnity, a high cost claim indemnity, a run-off cover indemnity or an allied health high cost claim indemnity payable to the liable person; or
under section 42.
The total amount recovered must not exceed the amount overpaid.
Subdivision E—Recovery of repayment or overpayment debt

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may collect money from a person who owes money to a person

content.p: What this section does

(1) This section allows the Chief Executive Medicare to collect money from a person who owes money to a person (the liable person) who has a debt to the Commonwealth under subsection 24(4), 34Q(6), 34T(3), 34ZJ(3), 34ZZW(6), 34ZZZ(3) or 41(3) (the repayment or overpayment debt).
The Chief Executive Medicare may give direction

(2) The Chief Executive Medicare may direct a person (the third party) who owes, or may later owe, money (the available money) to the liable person to pay some or all of the available money to the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with the direction. The Chief Executive Medicare must give a copy of the direction to the liable person.
Limit on directions
The direction must:
not require an amount to be paid to the Chief Executive Medicare at a time before it becomes owing by the third party to the liable person; and
specify a period of not less than 14 days within which the third party must comply with the direction.
If:
the repayment or overpayment debt relates to an exceptional claims indemnity or an allied health exceptional claims indemnity; and
the recipient and the practitioner referred to in subsection 34Q(1) or 34ZZW(1) are not the same person; and
the practitioner becomes the liable person; and
the direction was given to the recipient;
the direction ceases to have effect when the practitioner becomes the liable person.
Third party to comply
The third party commits an offence if the third party fails to comply with the direction.
Penalty: 20 penalty units.
The third party does not commit an offence against subsection (4) if the third party complies with the direction so far as the third party is able to do so.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
An offence against subsection (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Court orders

If a person is convicted of an offence in relation to a failure of the third party to comply with subsection (4), the court may (in addition to imposing a penalty on the convicted person) order the convicted person to pay to the Commonwealth an amount up to the amount involved in the failure of the third party.
Indemnity

Any payment made by the third party under this section is taken to have been made with the authority of the liable person and of all other persons concerned and the third party is indemnified for the payment.
Notice

If the whole of the repayment or overpayment debt of the liable person is discharged before any payment is made by the third party, the Chief Executive Medicare must immediately give notice to the third party of that fact.
If a part of the repayment or overpayment debt of the liable person is discharged before any payment is made by the third party, the Chief Executive Medicare must:
immediately give notice to the third party of that fact; and
make an appropriate variation to the direction; and
give a copy of the varied direction to the liable person.
When third party is taken to owe money
The third party is taken to owe money to the liable person if:
money is due or accruing by the third party to the liable person; or
the third party holds money for or on account of the liable person; or
the third party holds money on account of some other person for payment to the liable person; or
the third party has authority from some other person to pay money to the liable person;
whether or not the payment of the money to the liable person is dependent on a pre-condition that has not been fulfilled.

section.heading: Regulations may provide for subsidy scheme

content.p: The regulations may provide for one or more schemes for one or more of the following:
making payments to:
medical practitioners; or
medical indemnity insurers on behalf of medical practitioners;
to help those medical practitioners meet the cost of purchasing medical indemnity (whether such costs are incurred by way of MDO membership subscriptions, insurance premiums or otherwise);
making payments to:
medical practitioners; or
medical indemnity insurers on behalf of medical practitioners;
to help those medical practitioners meet the cost of paying run-off cover support payments;
making payments to medical indemnity insurers to help the medical indemnity insurers meet the cost of administering schemes provided for under paragraph (a).
Without limiting subsection (1), a scheme may make provision for:
the conditions that must be satisfied for a subsidy to be payable; and
the amount of a subsidy; and
the conditions that must be complied with by persons to whom a subsidy is paid; and
payments to medical indemnity insurers to reduce the costs of medical indemnity for medical practitioners; and
any amount payable to the Commonwealth to be recovered as a debt.
Without limiting paragraph (2)(a), a scheme may provide that a subsidy is to be paid only:
to medical practitioners working in particular areas of medical practice; or
for the purchase of particular kinds of medical indemnity.

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may request information

content.p: If the Chief Executive Medicare believes on reasonable grounds that a person is capable of giving information that is relevant to determining:
whether a subsidy is payable to a person under a scheme provided for under subsection 43(1); or
the amount of a subsidy that is payable to a person under a scheme provided for under subsection 43(1);
the Chief Executive Medicare may request the person to give the Chief Executive Medicare the information.
Note: Failure to comply with the request is an offence (see section 45).
The request:
must be made in writing; and
must state what information must be given to the Chief Executive Medicare; and
may require the information to be verified by statutory declaration; and
must specify a day on or before which the information must be given; and
must contain a statement to the effect that a failure to comply with the request is an offence.
The day specified under paragraph (d) must be at least 28 days after the day on which the request is made.

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may notify run-off cover credits

content.p: The Chief Executive Medicare may notify a medical practitioner of:
the practitioner’s run-off cover credit for a financial year; or
the amount worked out in relation to the practitioner under Step 2 of the Method Statement in subsection 34ZS(1) for a financial year; or
if a termination date for the run-off cover indemnity scheme has been set (see subsection 34ZB(3))—the practitioner’s total run-off cover credit.

section.heading: Failing to give information

content.p: This section applies if a person is given a request for information under:
subsection 27B(1); or
subsection 27C(3); or
subsection 34AB(1); or
subsection 34Y(1); or
subsection 34ZO(1); or
subsection 34ZZH(1); or
subsection 34ZZZE(1); or
subsection 38(1); or
subsection 44(1).
The person commits an offence if the person fails to comply with the request.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An individual is excused from complying with the request if the giving of the information might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Failing to notify

content.p: This section applies if section 25, 34J, 34U, 34ZK, 34ZT, 34ZU, 34ZZP or 34ZZZA requires a person to notify the Chief Executive Medicare of a matter within a particular period.
The person commits an offence if the person fails to notify the Chief Executive Medicare of the matter within that period.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.

An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability. However, strict liability does not apply to the physical element described in paragraph 34J(1)(b), 34U(1)(b), 34ZK(1)(b), 34ZZP(1)(b) or 34ZZZA(1)(b).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Failing to keep and retain records

content.p: This section applies if section 39 or 40 requires a person to keep records or to retain records for a particular period.
The person commits an offence if the person fails to keep the records or fails to retain the records for that period.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Failing to include required information in invoices

content.p: This section applies if section 34ZV applies to an invoice that a medical indemnity insurer gives to a person.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a medical indemnity insurer; and
the person gives such an invoice to another person; and
the invoice does not state the matters required by section 34ZV.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

(4) To avoid doubt, subsection 4B(3) of the Crimes Act 1914 applies to any offence against this section committed by a body corporate, as if an offence against that provision could be committed by a natural person.
Subsection (4) does not affect the meaning of any other offence against this Act.

section.heading: Appropriation

content.p: The Consolidated Revenue Fund is appropriated for the purposes of paying:
IBNR indemnities; and
high cost claim indemnities; and
exceptional claims indemnities; and
run-off cover indemnities; and
allied health high cost claim indemnities; and
allied health exceptional claims indemnities; and

amounts payable under regulations made for the purposes of section 27A (IBNR claims payments), 34AA (high cost claims payments), 34X (exceptional claims payments), 34ZN (run-off claims payments), 34ZZG (allied health high cost claims payments) or 34ZZZD (allied health exceptional claims payments); and
subsidies payable under a scheme provided for under subsection 43(1).

section.heading: Indemnity scheme payments disregarded for purposes of reinsurance contracts

content.p: If:
a contract is a contract of insurance:
between 2 insurers; or
between an insurer and an MDO that are not related bodies corporate; and
the contract is governed by the laws of a State or Territory;
the contract has effect as if the contract provided, and had at all times provided, that:
indemnity scheme payments; and
MDOs’ and insurers’ rights to indemnity scheme payments;
were to be disregarded for all purposes and, without limiting this, were to have no effect on the amounts payable under the contract by the insurer providing the insurance.
By force of this subsection, subsection (1) applies to a contract if it is entered into on or after the commencement of this Act.
By force of this subsection, subsection (1) applies to a contract if it was entered into before the commencement of this Act.

section.heading: Insurers may be required to provide information

content.p: The rules may require a medical indemnity insurer to provide to the Secretary information about any of the following:
premium costs for medical indemnity cover provided by contracts of insurance with the insurer;
the income of medical practitioners, or persons who practise an allied health profession, for whom contracts of insurance with the insurer provide medical indemnity cover;
the profitability of the insurer;
the insurer’s reinsurance arrangements and costs.

section.heading: Guide to the universal cover obligation provisions

content.p: This Part prevents medical indemnity insurers from refusing to provide medical indemnity cover for medical practitioners in relation to private medical practice, except in certain circumstances.
This Part also specifies when a medical indemnity insurer may require a medical practitioner to pay a risk surcharge.
Medical indemnity insurers must keep records and provide information in relation to these requirements.

section.heading: Winding up of medical indemnity insurer

content.p: This Part has effect subject to section 116 of the Insurance Act 1973.

Note: Under that section, a general insurer must not carry on insurance business after it starts to be wound up. A general insurer will not contravene this Part by refusing to enter into an insurance contract if the winding up of the insurer has started.

division.heading: Requirements in relation to providing professional indemnity cover

section.heading: Division applies for the purposes of the AFCA scheme

content.p: A medical indemnity insurer is not required to comply with this Division other than for the purposes of the AFCA scheme (within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001).
Note: A medical practitioner can make a complaint to AFCA about certain issues relating to medical indemnity insurance.

section.heading: Universal cover obligation

content.p: A medical indemnity insurer must not refuse to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover unless:
in relation to a contract of insurance between the practitioner and the insurer to provide professional indemnity cover, the practitioner:
(i) failed to comply with the duty of the utmost good faith (within the meaning of the Insurance Contracts Act 1984); or
failed to comply with the duty of disclosure (within the meaning of that Act); or
made a misrepresentation to the insurer during the negotiations for the contract but before it was entered into; or
failed to comply with a provision of the contract, including a provision with respect to payment of the premium; or
made a fraudulent claim under the contract; or

the practitioner places the public at risk of substantial harm in the practitioner’s private medical practice because the practitioner has an impairment (within the meaning of the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law); or
the practitioner’s private medical practice poses an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the public or patients; or
the practitioner poses an unreasonable risk of harm to members of the insurer’s staff because of persistent threatening or abusive behaviour towards members of the insurer’s staff; or
the practitioner has persistently failed to comply with reasonable risk management requirements of the insurer; or
the circumstances specified in the rules apply.

section.heading: Medical indemnity insurer to notify of refusal

content.p: If a medical indemnity insurer refuses to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover, the insurer must notify the practitioner in writing in accordance with any requirements specified in the rules.
Without limiting subsection (1), the rules may specify:
the information that must be included in the notification; and
a time within which the insurer must notify.

section.heading: Risk surcharge requirements

content.p: (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a medical indemnity insurer may require a medical practitioner (the practitioner) to pay, as part of the amount payable for professional indemnity cover provided by a contract of insurance with the practitioner, an amount (the risk surcharge):

to reflect that, because the practitioner engages, or has engaged, in conduct that deviates from good medical practice, the practitioner’s private medical practice is likely to pose a higher risk to patients than similar practices (see subsection (2)); or
in circumstances specified in the rules.

(2) The private medical practice of another medical practitioner (the comparison practitioner) is a similar practice if the insurer reasonably considers that the practitioner and the comparison practitioner have similar practice profiles for the purposes of calculating premiums for professional indemnity cover, except that the comparison practitioner does not engage, and has not engaged, in conduct that deviates from good medical practice.
The risk surcharge must not exceed the amount:
specified in the rules; or
worked out in accordance with a method specified in the rules.
The offer to enter into the contract of insurance to provide the professional indemnity cover must:
identify the amount of the risk surcharge; and
state the reason for requiring payment of the risk surcharge;
in accordance with any requirements specified in the rules.

section.heading: Medical indemnity insurer may be required to offer interim cover until complaint is finalised

content.p: A medical indemnity insurer must offer to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover if:
(a) a contract of insurance between the insurer and the practitioner provides professional indemnity cover (the initial cover); and
(b) the insurer refuses to enter into a contract of insurance with the practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover (the subsequent cover) starting after the initial cover ceases; and
the practitioner makes a complaint to AFCA in relation to the refusal; and
the initial cover, or professional indemnity cover provided as a result of an offer made for the purposes of this section, ceases before the complaint finalisation date.
The offer must comply with any requirements specified in the rules.
However, the insurer is not required to offer to enter into a contract of insurance that provides professional indemnity cover after the complaint finalisation date.
In this section:
complaint finalisation date means the earlier of:
the day the subsequent cover starts; and
the day 60 days after the complaint is finalised.
finalised: a complaint is finalised when:
the complaint is resolved by agreement between the insurer and the practitioner; or
the complaint is withdrawn; or
AFCA closes the complaint because:
it has excluded the complaint, or decided not to continue to consider the complaint, and the timeframe in which the practitioner may object to the decision has expired; or
it has made a preliminary assessment in relation to the complaint and the timeframe for requesting a determination of the complaint has expired; or
it has determined the complaint; or
the complaint otherwise ceases to be dealt with by AFCA.

section.heading: Records

content.p: The rules may require a medical indemnity insurer to keep records relating to the following:
a refusal by the insurer to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover;
a requirement by the insurer that a medical practitioner pay a risk surcharge.
Note: Failure to keep the records is an offence (see section 53A).
Records required by the rules must be retained for a period of 5 years (or any other period specified in the rules) starting on the day on which the records were created.
Note: Failure to retain the records is an offence (see section 53A).

section.heading: Failing to keep and retain records

content.p: This section applies if section 53 or rules made for the purposes of that section require a person to keep records or to retain records for a particular period.
The person commits an offence if the person fails to keep the records or fails to retain the records for that period.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Medical indemnity insurer must report annually

content.p: If, in a financial year, a medical indemnity insurer refuses to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover, the insurer must notify the Secretary within 2 months after the end of the financial year of:
the number of times in the financial year the insurer refused to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover; and
any other matter that relates to the insurer’s obligations under Division 2 and that is specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to notify is an offence (see section 53C).

If, in a financial year, a medical indemnity insurer requires a medical practitioner to pay a risk surcharge, the insurer must notify the Secretary within 2 months after the end of the financial year of:
the number of times in the financial year the insurer required a medical practitioner to pay a risk surcharge; and
any other matter that relates to the insurer’s obligations under Division 2 and that is specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to notify is an offence (see section 53C).
The Secretary may, by notifiable instrument, approve a form for the purposes of notification under subsection (1) or (2).
If the Secretary does so, the notification must be in the approved form.

Within 3 months after the end of the financial year, the Secretary must publish on the Department’s website any information notified under paragraph (1)(a) or (2)(a) in relation to the financial year.

section.heading: Failing to report

content.p: This section applies if section 53B requires a person to notify the Secretary of a matter within a particular period.
The person commits an offence if:
if the Secretary has approved a form for the purposes of the notification—the person fails to notify the Secretary of the matter in the approved form within that period; or
otherwise—the person fails to notify the Secretary of the matter within that period.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Secretary may request information

content.p: The Secretary may request a medical indemnity insurer to give the Secretary the following information, in the form requested by the Secretary:
the number of times in a period the insurer refused to enter into a contract of insurance with a medical practitioner to provide professional indemnity cover;
the number of times in a period the insurer required a medical practitioner to pay a risk surcharge;
any other information that relates to the insurer’s obligations under Division 2 and that is specified in the rules.
Note: Failure to comply with the request is an offence (see section 53E).
The request:
must be made in writing; and
may require the information to be verified by statutory declaration; and
must specify the day on or before which the information must be given; and
must contain a statement to the effect that a failure to comply with the request is an offence.
The day specified under paragraph (c) must be at least 28 days after the day on which the request is made.

section.heading: Failing to give information

content.p: This section applies if a person is given a request for information under section 53D.
The person commits an offence if the person fails to comply with the request.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: When run-off cover support payment must be paid

content.p: A run-off cover support payment that a person is liable to pay for a contribution year becomes due and payable on:
30 June in the contribution year; or

such other day as is specified in the rules as the payment day for the contribution year either generally for all people, for the class of people that includes the person or for the person, as the case may be.

section.heading: Late payment penalty

content.p: If:
a person is liable to pay a run-off cover support payment; and
the payment remains wholly or partly unpaid after it becomes due and payable;
the person is liable to pay a late payment penalty under this section.
The late payment penalty is calculated:
at the rate specified in the rules; and
on the unpaid amount of payment; and
for the period:
starting when the payment becomes due and payable; and
ending when the payment, and the penalty payable under this section in relation to the payment, have been paid in full.
Paragraph (c) has effect subject to subsection (3).
The person is not liable to pay a late payment penalty under subsection (1) for any period after the person’s death.
The Chief Executive Medicare may remit the whole or a part of an amount of late payment penalty if the Chief Executive Medicare considers that there are good reasons for doing so.
An application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of a decision of the Chief Executive Medicare not to remit, or to remit only part of, an amount of late payment penalty.

section.heading: Method of paying certain amounts

content.p: A run-off cover support payment must be paid to the Chief Executive Medicare.

section.heading: Refund of overpaid amounts

Appropriation
The Consolidated Revenue Fund is appropriated for the purpose of providing refunds under this section.

section.heading: Recovery of payment debt

content.p: A run-off cover support payment is a debt due to the Commonwealth.
A late payment penalty payable under section 65 is a debt due to the Commonwealth.
The Chief Executive Medicare may recover an amount referred to in subsection (1) or (3) as a debt by action in a court of competent jurisdiction.

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may collect money from a person who owes money to a person

content.p: What this section does

(1) This section allows the Chief Executive Medicare to collect money from a person who owes money to a person (the payment debtor) who has a debt to the Commonwealth under section 68 (a payment debt).
The Chief Executive Medicare may give direction

(2) The Chief Executive Medicare may direct a person (the third party) who owes, or may later owe, money (the available money) to the payment debtor to pay some or all of the available money to the Chief Executive Medicare in accordance with the direction. The Chief Executive Medicare must give a copy of the direction to the payment debtor.
Limit on directions
The direction must:
not require an amount to be paid to the Chief Executive Medicare at a time before it becomes owing by the third party to the payment debtor; and
specify a period of not less than 14 days within which the third party must comply with the direction.
Third party to comply
The third party commits an offence if the third party fails to comply with the direction.
Penalty: 20 penalty units.
The third party does not commit an offence against subsection (4) if the third party complies with the direction so far as the third party is able to do so.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
An offence against subsection (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Court orders

If a person is convicted of an offence in relation to a failure of the third party to comply with subsection (4), the court may (in addition to imposing a penalty on the convicted person) order the convicted person to pay to the Chief Executive Medicare an amount up to the amount involved in the failure of the third party.
Indemnity

Any payment made by the third party under this section is taken to have been made with the authority of the payment debtor and of all other persons concerned and the third party is indemnified for the payment.
Notice

If the whole of the payment debt of the payment debtor is discharged before any payment is made by the third party, the Chief Executive Medicare must immediately give notice to the third party of that fact.
If a part of the payment debt of the payment debtor is discharged before any payment is made by the third party, the Chief Executive Medicare must:
immediately give notice to the third party of that fact; and
make an appropriate variation to the direction; and
give a copy of the varied direction to the payment debtor.
When third party is taken to owe money
The third party is taken to owe money to the payment debtor if:
money is due or accruing by the third party to the payment debtor; or
the third party holds money for or on account of the payment debtor; or
the third party holds money on account of some other person for payment to the payment debtor; or
the third party has authority from some other person to pay money to the payment debtor;
whether or not the payment of the money to the payment debtor is dependent on a pre-condition that has not been fulfilled.

section.heading: Evidentiary certificates

content.p: The Chief Executive Medicare may issue a written certificate:
stating that a person is liable to pay:
a run-off cover support payment; or
a late payment penalty in relation to a run-off cover support payment; and
setting out particulars of the liability.
In any civil proceedings under, or arising out of, this Act or the medical indemnity payment legislation, a certificate under subsection (1) is prima facie evidence of the matters in the certificate.
A document purporting to be a certificate under subsection (1) must, unless the contrary is established, be taken to be such a certificate and to have been properly issued.
The Chief Executive Medicare may certify that a document is a copy of a certificate issued under subsection (1).
This section applies to the certified copy as if it were the original.
Subdivision E—Information gathering processes

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may request information

content.p: If the Chief Executive Medicare believes on reasonable grounds that a person is capable of giving information that is relevant to determining:
whether a person is liable to pay a run-off cover support payment; or
the amount of the run-off cover support payment a person is liable to pay; or
whether a person has medical indemnity cover provided by a contract of insurance with a particular medical indemnity insurer; or
whether a person is a member of a particular MDO;
the Chief Executive Medicare may request the person to give the Chief Executive Medicare the information.
Note: Failure to comply with the request is an offence (see section 73).
Without limiting subsection (1), any of the following persons may be requested to provide information under that subsection:
an MDO;
an insurer;
a member, or former member, of an MDO;
the legal personal representative of a person mentioned in paragraph (c).
The request:
must be made in writing; and
must state what information must be given to the Chief Executive Medicare; and
may require the information to be verified by statutory declaration; and
must specify the day on or before which the information must be given; and
must contain a statement to the effect that a failure to comply with the request is an offence.
The day specified under paragraph (d) must be at least 28 days after the day on which the request is made.

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare must be notified of a change in circumstances etc.

content.p: A person who:
is exempt from a run-off cover support payment; and
ceases to be exempt from the payment because:
the person’s circumstances change before the start of, or during, a contribution year; or
the person fails to satisfy a condition on which the exemption from the payment depends;
must notify the Chief Executive Medicare of that change in circumstances or that failure, as the case may be.
Note: Failure to notify is an offence (see section 74).
The notification must:
be in writing; and
set out details of the change in circumstances or failure of which the person is required to notify the Chief Executive Medicare under subsection (1); and
be given to the Chief Executive Medicare within 28 days after the day on which the person becomes aware of the change in circumstances or failure, as the case may be.

section.heading: Failing to give information

content.p: This section applies if a person is given a request for information under subsection 71(1).
The person commits an offence if the person fails to comply with the request.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An individual is excused from complying with the request if the giving of the information might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Failing to notify

content.p: This section applies if section 72 requires a person to notify the Chief Executive Medicare, within a particular period, of a matter.
The person commits an offence if the person fails to notify the Chief Executive Medicare of that matter within that period.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subsection (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: General administration of this Act and medical indemnity payment legislation

content.p: The Chief Executive Medicare has the general administration of this Act and the medical indemnity payment legislation.

section.heading: Additional functions of the Chief Executive Medicare

content.p: In addition to the functions of the Chief Executive Medicare under the Human Services (Medicare) Act 1973, the Chief Executive Medicare has such additional functions as are conferred on the Chief Executive Medicare under this Act and the medical indemnity payment legislation.

section.heading: Chief Executive Medicare may use computer programs to take administrative action

content.p: The Chief Executive Medicare may arrange for the use, under the Chief Executive Medicare’s control, of computer programs for any purposes for which the Chief Executive Medicare may or must take administrative action under this Act or a legislative instrument made under this Act.
Administrative action taken by the operation of a computer program under such an arrangement is, for the purposes of this Act, taken to be administrative action taken by the Chief Executive Medicare.

The Chief Executive Medicare may substitute a decision for a decision the Chief Executive Medicare is taken to have made under subsection (2) if the Chief Executive Medicare is satisfied that the decision made by the operation of the computer program is incorrect.
In this Act:
administrative action means any of the following:
making a decision;
exercising any power or complying with any obligation;
doing anything else that relates to making a decision or exercising a power or complying with an obligation.

section.heading: Delegation by Secretary

content.p: The Secretary may, in writing, delegate all or any of the functions or powers of the Secretary under this Act or a legislative instrument made under this Act to any of the following persons:
the Chief Executive Medicare;
(b) an SES employee, or an acting SES employee, in the Department or the Department administered by the Minister administering the Human Services (Centrelink) Act 1997.
Note: Sections 34AA to 34A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 contain provisions relating to delegations.
In performing a delegated function or exercising a delegated power, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the Secretary.

section.heading: Officers to observe secrecy

content.p: Definitions
In this section:
medical indemnity legislation means:
this Act; or
the medical indemnity payment legislation; or
(c) the repealed Medical Indemnity (Competitive Advantage Payment) Act 2005; or
(d) the repealed Medical Indemnity (UMP Support Payment) Act 2002.
officer means a person performing duties, or exercising powers or functions, under or in relation to, the medical indemnity legislation.
person to whom this section applies means a person who is or was an officer.
protected document means a document that:
is obtained or made by a person to whom this section applies in the course of, or because of, the person’s functions, powers or duties under or in relation to the medical indemnity legislation; and
contains information relating to a person’s affairs.
protected information means information that:

is disclosed to, or obtained by, a person to whom this section applies in the course of, or because of, the person’s functions, powers or duties under or in relation to the medical indemnity legislation; and
relates to a person’s affairs.
Offence
A person to whom this section applies commits an offence if:
the person:
makes a copy or other record of any protected information or of all or part of any protected document; or
discloses any protected information to another person; or
produces all or part of a protected document to another person; and
in doing so, is not acting in the performance of his or her duties, or in the exercise of his or her powers or functions, under the medical indemnity legislation; and
in doing so, is not acting for the purpose of enabling a person to perform functions under:
the medical indemnity legislation; or
(ii) the Health Insurance Act 1973; or
a medicare program; or
(iv) the National Health Act 1953; or
(v) the Private Health Insurance Act 2007.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Circumstances in which protected information and protected documents may be copied, recorded or divulged

Despite subsection (2), any of the following persons may make a copy or record of, or divulge to any other of the following persons, protected information or a protected document, for the purposes of monitoring, assessing or reviewing the operation of the medical indemnity legislation:
the Secretary;
the Chief Executive Medicare;
the Actuary;
the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority;
the Australian Securities and Investments Commission.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).

Despite subsection (2), any of the following persons may make a copy or record of, or divulge to any other of the following persons, protected information or a protected document, for the purposes of conducting, or assisting a person to conduct, the evaluation mentioned in section 78A:
a person mentioned in subsection (2A) of this section;
a person conducting the evaluation;
a person assisting a person to conduct the evaluation.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Despite subsection (2), the Secretary or the Chief Executive Medicare may:

if the Minister certifies, in writing, that it is necessary in the public interest that any protected information should be divulged, divulge that information to such person as the Minister directs; or
divulge any protected information to a person who, in the opinion of the Minister, is expressly or impliedly authorised by the person to whom the information relates to obtain it.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Despite subsection (2), the Secretary or the Chief Executive Medicare may divulge any protected information to an authority or person if:
the authority or person is specified in rules made for the purposes of this subsection; and
the information is information of a kind that may, in accordance with the rules, be provided to the authority or person.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
If protected information is divulged to an authority or person under subsection (2A), (2B), (3) or (4):
the authority or person; and
any person or employee under the control of the authority or person;

is, in respect of that information, subject to the same rights, privileges, obligations and liabilities under subsection (2) as if he or she were a person performing duties under the medical indemnity legislation and had acquired the information in the performance of those duties.
Despite subsection (2), an officer may make a record of information with the express or implied authorisation of the person to whom the information relates.
This section does not prohibit the divulging or communicating to a person of information that relates to the person.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subsection (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).

section.heading: Act not to apply in relation to State insurance within a State

content.p: If, but for this section, a provision of this Act:
would have a particular application; and
by virtue of having that application, would be a law with respect to State insurance not extending beyond the limits of the State concerned;
the provision is not to have that application.

section.heading: Evaluation of medical indemnity market

content.p: The Minister must cause to be conducted an actuarial evaluation of:
the stability of the medical indemnity insurance industry; and
the affordability of medical indemnity insurance.
The Minister must cause to be prepared a report of an evaluation under subsection (1).
The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament by 28 February 2021.

section.heading: Regulations

content.p: The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act;
and, in particular, prescribing penalties, not exceeding 10 penalty units, for offences against the regulations.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for the qualifications of actuaries preparing reports for the purposes of this Act.

section.heading: Rules

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by the rules; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
To avoid doubt, the rules may not do the following:
create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Act;
directly amend the text of this Act.

Rules that are inconsistent with the regulations have no effect to the extent of the inconsistency, but rules are taken to be consistent with the regulations to the extent that the rules are capable of operating concurrently with the regulations.
